sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) What is a Grignard reagent? (b) Write the reaction of CH3MgBr with water.
questions.answer: (a) An organomagnesium halide, RMgX, prepared from RX and Mg in dry ether. (b) CH3MgBr + H2O → CH4 + Mg(OH)Br.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) SN2 reaction takes place with inversion of configuration. (b) Haloarenes are more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution than haloalkanes.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – they are less reactive.

questions.q: Fill in: (a) The reaction of R–Cl with NaI in acetone is called the ______ reaction. (b) Chloroform is oxidised in air to ______.
questions.answer: (a) Finkelstein. (b) phosgene (COCl2).

questions.q: Match: (a) Wurtz reaction (b) Swarts reaction (c) Sandmeyer reaction with (i) AgF (ii) diazonium salt + CuCl (iii) RX + Na.
Write the products of (a) CH3CH2Br + aq. KOH and (b) CH3CH2Br + alc. KOH.
questions.answer: (a) Ethanol, CH3CH2OH. (b) Ethene, CH2=CH2.

questions.q: Name (a) the insecticide containing chlorine that is not biodegradable and (b) the compound used as an antiseptic.
questions.answer: (a) DDT. (b) Iodoform (CHI3).

questions.q: Write (a) the IUPAC name of CH3CHBrCH3 and (b) CH2=CHCl.
questions.answer: (a) 2-Bromopropane. (b) Chloroethene (vinyl chloride).

questions.q: Identify (a) the class of (CH3)3CBr and (b) the favoured mechanism.
questions.answer: (a) Tertiary haloalkane. (b) SN1.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is a Grignard reagent? How is it prepared?
questions.answer: An organomagnesium halide, R–Mg–X. It is prepared by reacting an alkyl or aryl halide with magnesium metal in dry ether: R–X + Mg → RMgX.

questions.q: Why is chlorobenzene less reactive than chloroethane in nucleophilic substitution?
questions.answer: In chlorobenzene the C–Cl bond has a partial double-bond character due to resonance, and the carbon is sp² hybridised (shorter, stronger bond); in addition, the phenyl cation is unstable.

questions.q: Distinguish between SN1 and SN2 reactions (two points).
questions.answer: SN1: two steps through a carbocation, rate depends on [RX] only, racemisation, tertiary halides favoured. SN2: single step, rate depends on [RX][Nu], inversion of configuration, primary halides favoured.

questions.q: How is chloroform stored and why?
questions.answer: In dark brown bottles filled to the brim because light and air oxidise it to poisonous phosgene gas, COCl2; about 1% ethanol is added to convert phosgene to harmless ethyl carbonate.

questions.q: Write the Sandmeyer reaction for the preparation of chlorobenzene from benzene diazonium chloride.
questions.answer: C6H5N2+Cl− + CuCl/HCl → C6H5Cl + N2 + CuCl.

questions.q: What is the Finkelstein reaction? Write an example.
questions.answer: Conversion of alkyl chlorides or bromides to iodides with NaI in dry acetone: CH3CH2Br + NaI → CH3CH2I + NaBr (NaBr precipitates).

questions.q: Why are haloalkanes insoluble in water though polar?
questions.answer: The energy released on forming new haloalkane–water attraction is less than that needed to break the hydrogen bonds of water and the dipole–dipole attractions of the haloalkane.

questions.q: Name two harmful effects of freons and DDT.
questions.answer: Freons deplete the ozone layer (cause skin cancer); DDT is non-biodegradable and accumulates in the food chain, harming birds and aquatic life.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the mechanism of the SN2 reaction of CH3Br with OH−.
questions.answer: The nucleophile OH− attacks the carbon from the side opposite to Br (backside) in a single step through a transition state in which C is partly bonded to both OH and Br; Br− leaves and the configuration is inverted; rate = k[CH3Br][OH−].

questions.q: Write the reactions of a Grignard reagent with (a) CO2 (b) methanal (c) a ketone.
questions.answer: (a) RMgX + CO2 → RCOOMgX → RCOOH (carboxylic acid). (b) RMgX + HCHO → RCH2OMgX → RCH2OH (primary alcohol). (c) RMgX + R'COR' → R3COMgX → tertiary alcohol after hydrolysis.

questions.q: How will you prepare (a) ethyl iodide from ethanol (b) chlorobenzene from aniline (c) 2-chloropropane from propene?
questions.answer: (a) C2H5OH + SOCl2 → C2H5Cl, then NaI/acetone gives C2H5I (or red P + I2). (b) Aniline → diazotisation (NaNO2/HCl, 273 K) → C6H5N2+Cl− → CuCl (Sandmeyer). (c) CH3CH=CH2 + HCl → CH3CHClCH3 (Markovnikov).

questions.q: Give reasons: (a) SN1 reactions are favoured by tertiary halides. (b) Haloalkanes have higher boiling points than alkanes of similar mass.
questions.answer: (a) The tertiary carbocation is stabilised by three alkyl groups (+I and hyperconjugation). (b) Haloalkanes are polar with dipole–dipole attractions and greater van der Waals forces than alkanes.

questions.q: Compare haloalkanes and haloarenes in respect of nucleophilic substitution, bond length of C–X and dipole moment.
questions.answer: Haloalkanes undergo nucleophilic substitution readily (C–X longer, 177 pm in CH3Cl, higher dipole moment 1.85 D); haloarenes resist it (C–X shorter, 169 pm in C6H5Cl, because of resonance and sp² carbon, lower dipole moment 1.69 D).

questions.q: Write short notes on chloroform and iodoform: preparation and uses.
questions.answer: Chloroform: ethanol/acetone with bleaching powder (haloform reaction), CH3CH2OH → CHCl3; solvent and used for making freon. Iodoform: ethanol + I2 + NaOH, CHI3 (yellow solid); used as an antiseptic for dressing wounds.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Explain halogenation of alkanes and write the mechanism briefly. (b) Compare haloalkanes and haloarenes with respect to nucleophilic substitution and give reasons. (c) Write the uses of methanol-derived and halogen compounds (CCl4, CHCl3).
questions.answer:
(a) Alkanes react with Cl2 in sunlight by a free-radical chain mechanism giving a mixture of haloalkanes: initiation (Cl2 → 2Cl•), propagation (Cl• + RH → R• + HCl; R• + Cl2 → RCl + Cl•), termination (radical coupling).
(b) Haloalkanes undergo nucleophilic substitution (SN1/SN2) readily; haloarenes do not because of the resonance partial double bond, sp² C–X, and repulsion of the nucleophile by the π cloud; nitro groups at o/p positions activate.
(c) CCl4: dry cleaning and fire extinguishers; CHCl3: solvent, preparation of freon and former anaesthetic.

questions.q: (a) Give the preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols, alkenes and halogen exchange. (b) Write the products of RX with aq. KOH, alc. KOH, KCN and AgCN.
questions.answer:
(a) From alcohols: R–OH + SOCl2 → RCl + SO2 + HCl; from alkenes: addition of HX (Markovnikov); halogen exchange: Finkelstein (RCl + NaI → RI) and Swarts (RCl + AgF → RF).
(b) aq. KOH → R–OH; alc. KOH → alkene; KCN → R–CN (nitrile); AgCN → R–NC (isocyanide).

questions.q: (a) Discuss SN1 and SN2 mechanisms with stereochemistry. (b) Predict the order of reactivity of CH3Br, CH3CH2Br, (CH3)2CHBr, (CH3)3CBr in SN2 and SN1.
questions.answer:
(a) SN2: backside attack, concerted, inversion (Walden), rate = k[RX][Nu]. SN1: ionisation to a planar carbocation then attack on either face, racemisation of an optically active halide, rate = k[RX].
(b) SN2: CH3Br > CH3CH2Br > (CH3)2CHBr > (CH3)3CBr (steric hindrance). SN1: (CH3)3CBr > (CH3)2CHBr > CH3CH2Br > CH3Br (carbocation stability).

questions.q: (a) Describe the Sandmeyer and Gattermann reactions and the Wurtz–Fittig reaction with equations. (b) State the environmental effects of CFCs and DDT.
questions.answer:
(a) Sandmeyer: ArN2+Cl− + CuCl → ArCl + N2 (similarly CuBr). Gattermann: ArN2+X− + Cu/HX → ArX. Wurtz–Fittig: ArX + RX + 2Na → Ar–R + 2NaX (dry ether).
(b) CFCs release Cl atoms in the stratosphere that destroy ozone; DDT does not degrade, accumulates in fatty tissue and food chains and reduces the eggshell thickness of birds.
